mbm-2651.clue: My little plates have four names.
mbm-2651.quote: I painted each of my smallest weight plates the color of a season. I save spring for last, whatever the month. That tiny extra lift feels possible even in February.

mbm-2652.clue: The blue scarf has a mind of its own.
mbm-2652.quote: I juggled two balls and a silk scarf outside a bakery. The warm air over the door lifted the blue scarf higher than the balls. I stood there catching the same little patch of sky all morning.

mbm-2653.clue: Our tour guide only showed us ceilings.
mbm-2653.quote: I asked a street painter what visitors missed in her town. She turned my map upside down and pointed above the shop doors. I spent the afternoon sketching painted stars and vines under the balconies. My neck ached for two days and I filled six pages.

mbm-2654.clue: One pawn is older than I am.
mbm-2654.quote: Our park set has a dark wooden pawn worn almost round. The old man who taught me said he started with it too. I move that one gently even when I'm losing.

mbm-2655.clue: I made a new friend with half a cracker.
mbm-2655.quote: The fair's soup-eating contest had no prize for garnishes. The girl beside me split her last cracker in two anyway. We tapped the halves together like little glasses before the whistle.

mbm-2656.clue: I draw the train twice before I finish my tea.
mbm-2656.quote: On our branch line the track loops around a little hill. I sketch the front carriage going in and the back carriage coming out. The stationmaster can tell whether the train was late by how cold my tea looks in the drawing.

mbm-2657.clue: The paddle has a white line just for me.
mbm-2657.quote: My first rafting guide wrapped a stripe round the paddle shaft to help me find my grip. I know the ridge by touch now. When my cousin tried rafting I put a stripe on hers.

mbm-2658.clue: I asked the bridge to sing bass.
mbm-2658.quote: I sang one long note under the stone arch by the river and the echo came back low and rough. I record our duet on a little tape. The bridge always insists I sing first.

mbm-2659.clue: My oldest tent has a thumb-size window.
mbm-2659.quote: A spark made a hole in the fly before I owned it. I patched it with clear plastic. Now there's one bright star I can see from my pillow when all the flaps are tied.

mbm-2660.quote: The pie contest served each slice on a paper plate a local kid had drawn on. I ate slowly so the little green dinosaur appeared feet first. The fast eaters missed the best part.

mbm-2661.clue: I know which square came from the top drawer.
mbm-2661.quote: The top-drawer napkins at my aunt's had a lavender scent. I sewed one into our quilt. When the summer sun warms it on the line I still get a breath of her kitchen.

mbm-2662.clue: A lucky strike goes in the sugar jar.
mbm-2662.quote: My grandpa used to sketch bowling pins on old sugar packets when he bowled well. I found the packets in a jar and drew my first strike on a fresh one. I slipped it between his.

mbm-2663.clue: I sweep a circle before I start.
mbm-2663.quote: At the outdoor martial arts class I clear pine needles with a straw broom. The cleared circle is a different shape every week. My teacher says a good stance fits all of them.

mbm-2664.clue: I have a constellation only my family can see.
mbm-2664.quote: We camp under tall pines that hide half the sky. By torchlight my brother poked our own pattern of stars into the lid of a tin. The tent ceiling has shown that same crooked spoon every trip.

mbm-2665.clue: I went shopping for a lid.
mbm-2665.quote: I had a fine old teapot with no lid. At the market I found one painted with yellow ducks. The teapot has roses. The seller called it a garden pond and gave me a fair price.

mbm-2666.clue: You can see the train go by in my tea.
mbm-2666.quote: My window at the crossing faces the tracks. I set my cup on the sill and sketch the ripples while the freight train passes. The longest train made a drawing like a chrysanthemum.

mbm-2667.clue: My bishop is a late riser.
mbm-2667.quote: At dawn our park table sits in shade except for one diagonal of sun. I put the white bishop on it and let the wood warm before our first game. My opponent calls that an opening advantage.

mbm-2668.clue: I take my lunch in a hollow.
mbm-2668.quote: My favorite hiking spot is where a fallen tree left a dip just my size. I sit there with soup and watch everyone's boots pass at eye level. The only one who spotted me was a dog.

mbm-2669.clue: I put the loud page in a quiet drawer.
mbm-2669.quote: When two characters shout at each other I write the scene on bright orange paper. I can open the desk drawer in the morning and see exactly which pair still owe each other an apology.

mbm-2670.clue: The toy shop sold me an empty box.
mbm-2670.quote: I asked a market stallholder for the box his wind-up birds came in. There was a blue sky painted inside. My little sister hung it over her bed with one paper bird flying through.

mbm-2671.clue: My broom has the captain's old whistle mark.
mbm-2671.quote: The wood on my curling broom has a pale ring from our captain's whistle loop. I leave it bare when I polish the handle. My hand always rests near the mark when we need a calm shot.

mbm-2672.clue: I kept my eyes on the pink helmet.
mbm-2672.quote: The first hard bend in our rafting trip made me stare at the foam. Our guide wore a vivid pink helmet. Find the pink, catch the paddle rhythm, breathe. By the last bend I was laughing.

mbm-2673.clue: The painted bird has one real feather.
mbm-2673.quote: I painted the pigeon outside my window so often that the windowsill filled with sketches. When a loose feather blew onto the wet paint I left it there. He finally signed a portrait himself.

mbm-2674.clue: My sister hangs her little boat on a hook.
mbm-2674.quote: I tooled a little boat on the back of my sister's leather belt. She only sees it when she hangs the belt on a hook. At the end of every long shift her boat is waiting.

mbm-2675.clue: Mum can count my last rep from the kitchen.
mbm-2675.quote: Mum keeps a little gym behind her cafe. She watches my last set between lunch orders. Nobody else says nice lift and two grilled cheeses in the same breath with quite so much authority.
